harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/legacy2/numeric-record-ordering/bin/merge. It now performs CSV-aware numeric ordering, emits one header, collapses identical duplicates, rejects conflicting duplicates with details, and atomically preserves the existing output on failure. The repair persisted across the required node1 restart. OS and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced the raw cat/sort implementation with a Python 3 standard-library CSV merger.
Published merged.csv containing IDs 2, 10, and 100 in numeric order.
Verified the quoted field "Tape, wide" remains intact and duplicate ID 2 collapses.
Tested conflicting ID 2; publication stopped and merged.csv remained byte-identical.
Restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed and all merge behavior recovered.

evidence.requirement: Numeric ordering, valid CSV, one header, and identical-duplicate collapse
evidence.summary: Semantic checks confirmed one header, IDs ordered 2/10/100, quoted comma preservation, and one retained copy of identical ID 2.

evidence.requirement: Conflicting duplicates stop publication and explain the conflict
evidence.summary: Conflict tests exited 1, identified transaction ID 2 and both differing records, and showed identical before/after output hashes.

evidence.requirement: Existing output remains intact after a failed merge
Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Before and after repair/restart, node1 remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID f1afbc7f-689a-477e-99b4-358a1d1d8226 was captured; the safe reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to e4c5407b-4a40-400a-a391-a5524270f126, system state returned to running, persisted data matched, and both successful and conflicting merge paths passed.
